gedankt.en: thank you, given the thanks («danken» participle)

texto: In German there are verbs with dativa (**helfen**, **danken**, **gratulieren**). In passive the dative is maintained and the phrase begins with it, with **es** or without real subject: **Mir wurde geholfen** (they helped me). Literally: «I was helped.».
With «es» in front, it is used to enter the phrase: **Es wurde mir geholfen** (helped me; helped me).

With intransitive verbs that do not carry an accusative complement, such as **helfen**, **danken** and **gratulieren**, the passive is usually impersonal and retains the dative: **Mir wurde gedankt** (I was thanked), **Ihm wurde gratuliert** (they congratulated him). The rule does not apply to all verbs with dative: if the verb also carries an accusative object, that object may become subject to the passive: **Der Chef gab mir den Schlüssel** → **Der Schlüssel wurde mir gegeben** (the boss gave me the key → gave me the key). Eye with the false friend: in German **gedankt werden** means «to receive the thanks».
